observations.statement: Plan and Deep Plan are project-file read-only, create a Puppet Master-controlled draft by default, require approval before execution, and execute only under regular or yolo.
Debug Mode defines eight ordered phases and requires revalidation for identity drift, recorded verification, and cleanup of temporary instrumentation.
The workflow display enum and canonical runtime mode are explicitly separated, including normalization of debug to regular or yolo and deep_plan to plan.
Provider, model, effort, and worktree changes apply to a next turn, while queued entries are represented by a separate field set containing text and attachment references.
Message controls use most-recent-user scope, a maximum-two FIFO queue, cancellation events, and soft supersession with retained audit/export tombstones.
Web commands use explicit subcommands and normalized input shapes, while skill invocation converges from GUI, slash command, and natural-language paths.
Chat-level and application-level ELI5 toggles have different defaults and scopes and are intended to be stored independently.
The Git/GitHub boundary distinguishes local and hosted operations and requires cross-domain handoff identity preservation.

candidate_findings.title: Planning approval is not bound to an immutable artifact revision
candidate_findings.claim: The capsule requires approval and later reuse of the approved plan/TODO state, but it defines no artifact identifier, revision or digest, approving principal and scope, expiry, or execution-time equality check. It therefore does not establish that the state executed is the state the user approved.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A draft, TODO set, runtime posture, or target could change after approval or while execution is queued, allowing execution under stale or mismatched authority.

candidate_findings.title: Queued turns lack an immutable execution-target snapshot
candidate_findings.claim: Runtime controls apply on the next turn, but the enumerated queue-entry fields omit provider, model, effort, workflow/runtime mode, permission posture, project, and worktree identity. The capsule does not choose enqueue-time versus dequeue-time resolution or require requested/effective identities to be persisted per queued turn.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A deferred message can execute with credentials, model behavior, permissions, or a worktree different from those visible when the user queued it, including mutations in the wrong checkout.

candidate_findings.title: Cancellation timeout has no fence against overlapping queued execution
candidate_findings.claim: The only stated queue-advancement gate is recording either `chat_run.cancelled` or `chat_run.cancel_timeout` after three seconds. The capsule does not say that `cancel_timeout` blocks advancement, revokes mutation leases, quarantines the thread, or proves the prior model, tool, and subagent activity has stopped.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The next FIFO item could begin while timed-out work is still mutating files or external systems, producing races, duplicate actions, and corrupted GUI status.

candidate_findings.title: Edit and Resend hide transcript state without compensating completed side effects
candidate_findings.claim: The UI language says later history or work is discarded, but the defined operation only marks later messages, tool cards, and draft operation cards as superseded and hides them. No rollback or compensation is defined for completed shell commands, file edits, Git operations, GitHub actions, web actions, or other external tools; `/revert` is separately constrained to a file-mutation restore path.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Users can be shown a rewound transcript while supposedly discarded mutations remain live, causing repeated or contradictory actions and false confidence about repository or remote state.

candidate_findings.title: No user deletion or purge contract exists despite retained tombstones
candidate_findings.claim: The capsule explicitly removes the delete action and retains superseded content with source references in audit/export views, but it provides no purge route, retention duration, access-control rule, redaction behavior, or disclosure that Edit and Resend do not delete sensitive content.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Secrets, personal data, or regulated content may remain exportable after the user reasonably believes an edit or rewind removed it.

candidate_findings.title: The claimed closed debug lifecycle lacks closed failure transitions
candidate_findings.claim: The phase list is a linear happy-path sequence, not a closed transition model. The capsule does not define permitted transitions or terminal outcomes for target-not-found, unsupported instrumentation, permission denial, failed reproduction, repair refusal, failed verification, cancellation, restart during repair, or cleanup failure. It also permits missing verification to map to `failed_cleanup`, conflating verification and cleanup status.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Implementations can skip phases, strand investigations, or report different terminal states for identical failures, preventing deterministic UI behavior and lifecycle tests.

candidate_findings.title: YOLO disclosure has no explicit authority ceiling
candidate_findings.claim: The surface defines YOLO as maximum permissions with no prompts but does not state an inherited non-bypassable safety ceiling, distinguish local from network or hosted actions, define credential and secret handling, require a high-risk warning, identify the exact session scope, or specify immediate revocation behavior.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The UI can imply unlimited authority while different providers or tools enforce different limits, and users can enable destructive remote behavior without understanding its effective scope.

candidate_findings.title: The worktree control conflates binding with mutation-capable actions
candidate_findings.claim: The same dropdown exposes create, unbind, merge, PR, and remove, while the following rule says changing worktree binding takes effect on the next turn. The capsule does not distinguish immediate actions from deferred binding changes or define confirmations, permission checks, idempotency, cancellation, and partial-failure states for merge, PR, or removal.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A user cannot reliably tell whether a selection merely changes the next-turn target or immediately mutates local or hosted repository state.

candidate_findings.title: Crawl and map bounds lack deterministic defaults and hard limits
candidate_findings.claim: The web schema makes `max_pages`, `max_depth`, and `same_origin_only` optional, gives no defaults or allowed ranges, and exposes direct slash grammar containing only a URL. This conflicts with the capsule's stated deterministic-default posture.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Implementations may perform divergent, unexpectedly large, or off-origin traversals, consuming excessive time, tokens, bandwidth, and provider quota.

candidate_findings.title: Absolute URL normalization is not a network-security boundary
candidate_findings.claim: Fetch, extract, crawl, and map require normalization to an absolute URL, but the capsule states no allowed schemes, loopback/private/link-local restrictions, redirect policy, DNS-rebinding defense, credential-forwarding policy, response-size ceiling, or handling of URLs containing secrets.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Web commands can become an SSRF, local-service probing, credential leakage, or resource-exhaustion path even when parsing and absolute-URL normalization succeed.

candidate_findings.title: Natural-language skill dispatch lacks an explicit authority and disclosure contract
candidate_findings.claim: GUI, `/skill`, and natural-language requests converge on `invoke_skill`, and the field vocabulary acknowledges high-side-effect behavior, but the capsule does not require pre-dispatch disclosure of the resolved skill identity, version, source, parsed arguments, capabilities, requested permissions, or whether natural-language matching requires confirmation.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Ambiguous or prompt-injected text could invoke a powerful skill without the user seeing which executable capability and arguments were selected.

candidate_findings.title: Chat ELI5 persistence scope remains nondeterministic
candidate_findings.claim: Chat ELI5 is described as a `per-chat or per-session` flag while the two toggles are said to be stored separately. The capsule does not choose one persistence scope or define restore, duplicate-thread, multi-window, account-sync, migration, and precedence behavior.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The system prompt can change unexpectedly after resume or in another window, and different clients can apply incompatible defaults despite the stated deterministic-default rule.

candidate_findings.title: Provider and model controls omit stale and failed-resolution states
candidate_findings.claim: Models are dynamically discovered and cached and selections take effect on a future turn, but the capsule defines no loading, stale-cache, discovery-failed, credential-expired, model-removed, unsupported-effort, fallback-selected, or requested-versus-effective mismatch state for the controls.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The header can display a selection that cannot run or silently resolves to another identity, leaving users unable to understand or recover from provider changes.

candidate_findings.title: Archive command reservation is internally ambiguous
candidate_findings.claim: The canonical non-overridable reserved list omits `/archive`, while the following thread-management rule groups `/revert/share/archive` as commands. The capsule does not establish whether `/archive` is active, reserved, an alias, or prose shorthand.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Autocomplete, custom-command collision handling, migration, and dispatch implementations can disagree about whether users may override or invoke `/archive`.

candidate_findings.title: Transient queue failure recovery and attachment cleanup are incomplete
candidate_findings.claim: Queue state is intentionally not restored, and the queue record contains a generic `state`, `text_ref`, and `attachment_refs`, but no allowed state set, transition table, crash-discard receipt, pre-reload warning, text or attachment reclamation rule, or recovery UX is defined.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Queued work can disappear after restart while referenced drafts or attachments leak storage, and the UI cannot deterministically distinguish sent, cancelled, lost, and orphaned entries.

candidate_findings.title: Project or repository disappearance has no active-run transition
candidate_findings.claim: The capsule says project-bound capabilities do not work without a selected project and hides the worktree control when no Git repository exists, but it defines no freeze, cancel, rebind, or attention-required transition when a project, repository, or bound worktree disappears while a response or queued item exists.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: An active or deferred operation may continue against stale paths, fall back to an unintended target, or lose its only recovery control without an honest status change.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: Runtime normalization is explicit for Ask, Agent, Debug, Plan, Deep Plan, and specialized execution overlays; Debug does not mint a new runtime-mode enum and Deep Plan retains display identity while using plan posture.
The capsule explicitly prevents Plan and Deep Plan from mutating project files before approval and prohibits execution under plan posture.
Debug target drift, restarts, adapter replacement, and evidence expiry require visible revalidation, and verification plus cleanup are mandatory before resolved status.
The queue has an explicit FIFO capacity of two, Stop does not implicitly clear it, cancellation emits named events with a three-second grace interval, and transcript rewrites retain tombstones.
Chat-level and app-level ELI5 behavior is explicitly separated, with different defaults and an explicit prohibition on changing generated-document style.
Bare `/web` is help-only, executable intents require explicit subcommands, URL parse failure shows usage rather than guessing, and command IDs are enumerated.
Local Git and hosted GitHub requests are explicitly distinguished, silent reinterpretation is prohibited, and cross-domain handoff identity must be preserved.

exact_evidence_refs.excerpt: > **Compliance:** This document follows `Plans/DRY_Rules.md` and references SSOT contracts in `Plans/Contracts_V0.md`. Naming: “Puppet Master” only. No open questions; deterministic defaults per `Plans/Decision_Policy.md`.

Planning-time rules for both `Plan` and `Deep Plan` remain:
- planning is read-only with respect to project files
- any planning artifact created during the planning run is a Puppet Master-controlled draft, not a normal repo file by default
- approval is required before the assistant can switch from planning into execution
- execution after approval reuses the approved plan/TODO state and runs under `regular` or `yolo`, never under `plan`
- queueing affects only post-approval execution, never the planning-time read-only run

**Closed debug phase model:**
1. `target_binding` — bind or confirm the exact debug target.
2. `baseline_capture` — capture starting state, reproduction preconditions, and relevant runtime identity.
3. `instrumentation` — add only the minimum temporary instrumentation required for diagnosis.
4. `reproduction` — reproduce or confirm the issue against the bound target.
5. `analysis` — reason over the bounded evidence set.
6. `repair` — apply the smallest viable fix or remediation step.
7. `verification` — verify whether the issue is resolved.
8. `cleanup` — remove temporary instrumentation, temporary env/config, and temporary debug-only runtime state.

- Before any mutation-capable step after `target_binding`, the assistant MUST revalidate the investigation when the target identity, bound worktree/branch, requested/effective runtime identity, auth/account binding, or instrumentation availability has drifted.
- The normal automated path covers target discovery and selection, browser or `/test/process` reproduction, evidence capture, tracer `/instrumentation` install or activation, analysis, tentative fix, automated verification, and cleanup or rollback.
- Revalidation is also mandatory after target restarts, debug adapter/session replacement, or evidence expiry that invalidates the current hypothesis.
- A revalidation gate surfaces an explicit reason in the Investigation Context; it MUST NOT silently continue as though the earlier target binding were still valid.
- `verification` is not optional. A fix attempt without a recorded verification result remains `attention_required` or `failed_cleanup`, not `resolved`.
- `cleanup` is the terminal mutation-capable phase for an otherwise successful investigation. Temporary instrumentation may persist only when the user explicitly preserves it or a preservation/hold rule says it must stay.

The chat surface exposes both workflow overlays and runtime execution posture. Only the runtime posture normalizes into the canonical run-envelope `mode` used by `Plans/Run_Modes.md`.

For Assistant display, message metadata, and context-detail filtering, the workflow-mode enum is closed to `ask | agent | debug | plan | deep_plan`. `debug` remains a workflow overlay that normalizes to `regular` by default or to `yolo` only by explicit opt-in; `deep_plan` remains a first-class workflow/display identity even though the underlying run-envelope runtime posture is still `plan`. Subordinate behavior/profile fields may describe investigation or planning depth, but they do not replace this workflow-mode enum.

| UI/workflow state | Canonical runtime mode | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Ask | `ask` | Always read-only. |
| Plan / Deep Plan (before execution) | `plan` | Always read-only; produces planning output only. |
| Agent with standard approvals | `regular` | Standard execute posture. |
| Debug with standard approvals | `regular` | Debug overlay stays visible; runtime stays execution-capable without minting a new enum. |
| Debug with explicit YOLO posture | `yolo` | Power-user opt-in only. |
| Interview / BrainStorm / Crew execution with standard approvals | `regular` | Specialized overlays do not create extra runtime-mode enum values. |
| Explicit YOLO execution outside Debug | `yolo` | Full-automation posture. |

**Requires a project:** many assistant capabilities (for example `@` file mention, project-scoped commands, local browser targets, run/debug presets, and project-bound debugging) do not work when no project is selected. When no project is selected, only application-wide rules and non-project target kinds remain available.

The chat window must allow the user to change platform, model, reasoning/effort, and worktree binding without leaving the chat.

Required controls (placement: chat header strip, same area as the context indicator / mode controls):

| Control | Requirement |
|---|---|
| **Provider** | Dropdown listing available provider entries from the account-bound Provider -> models registry. Selection applies to the current thread and the next turn. Data comes from Models/Multi-Account/Contracts capability snapshots; no hardcoding and no legacy `platform_specs` authority. |
| **Model** | Dropdown listing models for the currently selected provider entry. Models are dynamically discovered where supported, cached, and user-manageable via Settings or a manage-models entrypoint. Fallback model lists come from the shared provider/model registry and capability resolver, never `platform_specs::fallback_model_ids(platform)`. |
| **Reasoning / effort** | Shown only when the active platform supports it. Applies to the next turn rather than interrupting an in-flight response. |
| **Worktree** | Icon button (rightmost in header strip, after Reasoning/effort). Dropdown for per-thread worktree binding: create, unbind, merge, PR, remove. Visual states: unbound (dimmed glyph), bound-clean (lit glyph), bound-dirty (lit glyph + dot indicator), bound-conflict (lit glyph + warning triangle). Hidden when the active project has no git repository. Full specification in the "Worktrees in Assistant" section below. |

A *turn* is one complete user -> agent exchange: one user message plus the full agent response, including tool calls and final result. Changing platform, model, effort, or worktree binding takes effect on the next turn. If the user changes settings while a response is streaming, the current response completes with the prior selection.

- **What:** A toggle **in the chat UI** that, when **on**, instructs the Assistant to explain technical terms and steps in simpler terms and with more detail (ELI5 = "Explain Like I'm 5") in **that chat**.
- **Default:** **OFF** (Expert/default LLM behavior). By default, no extra "explain simply" instruction is added.
- **Scope:** Affects **Assistant chat behavior only** (explanations, follow-ups, teaching in the conversation).
- **Does NOT affect:** Interviewer **documentation writing style**. When the interview generates PRD, AGENTS.md, requirements, or other docs, chat ELI5 is **ignored**; generated docs remain technical and precise for agent consumption.
- **Implementation:** Chat ELI5 is a per-chat or per-session flag. When building the system prompt or instruction block for the Assistant, append an ELI5 instruction only for that session; do not pass it into interview document-generation prompts.

### 2.2 Application-level ELI5 (app-wide)

- **What:** A **separate** toggle at **application/settings level** labeled **Interaction Mode (Expert/ELI5)**. When ELI5 is active, **tooltips** and **interviewer responses** (in the Interview flow) are longer and simpler.
- **Default:** **ON** (ELI5). New users see simpler copy by default.
- **Scope:** Affects **tooltips** across the app (e.g. Config, Dashboard, Chat) and **interviewer Q&A responses** (the text the interview agent shows when asking questions or giving feedback). Does **not** change generated documentation (PRD, AGENTS.md, etc.).
- **Independent of chat ELI5:** A user can have app ELI5 on (simpler tooltips and interviewer text) and chat ELI5 off (technical Assistant answers in chat), or the reverse. The two toggles are stored and applied separately.
- **Dual-copy rule:** Every in-scope authored copy item in this plan (tooltips/help, interviewer Q&A copy, and chat style instruction copy) must define both **Expert** and **ELI5** variants. Track and audit against `Plans/FinalGUISpec.md` §7.4.0.

- **YOLO mode:** Chat runs with maximum permissions; no permission prompts. Agent can execute, edit, and run tools without asking. User accepts full automation for that session.
- **Regular mode:** Agent asks for permission before executing or editing. User-facing approval follows the canonical ladder: `deny`, `once`, `for session`, `always`.
- **Persistence:** Mode is a per-session or per-chat setting (configurable in chat UI or settings). `for session` does not persist across app restarts; durable approval/default behavior is owned by `Plans/Permissions_System.md`.

Core rules:
- Message controls are locked to most-recent-user scope, queued-message FIFO semantics, explicit rewind/discard behavior, always-visible code-block copy, mandatory subagent disclosure, and transient queue state that is not restored across reload or restart.
- Ordinary fenced code blocks render an always-visible copy button; the copy affordance/behavior may add emphasis or secondary controls on hover/focus, but copy availability must not depend on hover-only discovery.
- The message-stream control row keeps a thread-visible copy-icon on user and assistant messages, exposes `/submit`/stop morphing in the composer, and scopes `Stop`, `Edit`, and `Resend` to the most recent user-sent message only. `/edit/delete` is retired as a shorthand: edit and resend are supported, but no delete action is exposed. This is the message-control SSOT for most-recent-message controls.
- `/control` is a retired generic shorthand in this section; use `message-control` plus the concrete Stop/Edit/Resend, send-stop morph, copy-icon, and jump controls.
- The normalized message action labels are `Copy`, `Edit`, and `Resend`: `Copy` appears on every message, while `Edit` and `Resend` appear only on the most recent user-sent message. `Resend` replays that message and discards later generated history or work.
- Stop, Edit, and Resend render as icon buttons with accessible names rather than long text buttons in compact message-control rows.
- When the user is scrolled away from the bottom, chat shows a jump-to-latest / jump-to-bottom control with an unseen-count badge; auto-follow resumes when the user returns to the bottom.
- Message-control canon keeps `/steer` as the queue-area and interrupt path, not a message rewrite action. Only the most recent user message exposes Edit and `/resend`; resend replays as-is after rewinding later `/history`, stop cancels the active-run, `/steer/interrupt` remains distinct from stop, resend, `/follow`, and follow-up queuing, and controls expire after the next user message. `/follow` auto-follows only while the user is at the bottom and re-enables when the jump-to-latest action returns to bottom.
- Inline interactive visuals may be summoned by natural-language requests, but they render through the visual-module host contract and remain bounded thread content rather than arbitrary runtime heap state.
- Code-block actions include copy by default and may expose `/open-in-editor` only when a filename/path binding exists.
- The queued-message capacity is max 2 in FIFO order; when the queue is full, the composer must surface a queue full state and require the user to send, edit, or cancel an existing queued message before adding another.
- Stop does NOT clear the queue

- queue state is transient and is not restored across reload or restart
- Stop becomes disabled when a run completes and no next message is queued
- Edit restores content into composer and discards later history/work
- Resend retries the most recent message and discards later history/work
- Stop first records `chat_run.cancel_requested`, sends cancel to the active model/tool/subagent leases, waits up to `cancel_grace_ms = 3000`, and then records `chat_run.cancelled` or `chat_run.cancel_timeout` before queued messages may advance.
- Edit and Resend perform a soft history mutation: later generated messages, tool cards, and draft operation cards are marked `superseded_by_message_id` and hidden from the active transcript, while audit/export views retain tombstones and source refs.
- Queue entries use `{queue_entry_id, thread_id, draft_message_id, enqueued_at, position, state, text_ref, attachment_refs[], source_composer_id}`; when the max-2 queue is full, the new draft remains in the composer and the send action is disabled with `queue_full` until the user removes or sends an existing entry.

The chat footer owns the send/stop morph, queued-message affordance, and visible latest-message actions, while files-touched output stays a compact projection of edit/diff activity rather than a second transcript.

Rules:
- Queue UI shows FIFO order, pending count, and stop/interrupt state without restoring transient queued text after reload or restart.
- Files touched entries show `Read:` / `Edited:` labels, diff counts, and click-to-open editor routes through the shared operation-card and editor target contracts.
- Footer controls, queue state, and files-touched summaries must remain synchronized with operation cards so command-card, web/search, terminal, and diff activity do not fork separate status models.

### 5.3 Git & GitHub command boundary
Git and GitHub prefixes remain reserved and route into the canonical source-control and GitHub command surfaces rather than to user-defined command overrides.

Boundary rules:
- `/git ...` and natural-language requests for local repository work route to the Git/Source Control command family: status, diff, branch/worktree, commit, merge, revert, stash, and other local repository operations.
- `/github ...` and natural-language requests for PR, issue, Actions, workflow, review, comment, release, or hosted-repo administration route to the GitHub command family.
- The assistant MUST NOT silently reinterpret a Git request as a GitHub request, or vice versa, just because one path appears easier.
